I have not found the exact markdown file in the file library yet, only related context artifacts, so I’m checking local sources and will state that limitation if unresolved.

AGENDA  Establish source boundary: I treated ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_V1.md as the controlling Project Source target, but the exact verbatim file was not retrievable from the available project files. This review is therefore conservative and grounded in the retrieved project-source summaries plus adjacent repo evidence.  Review whether Git-managed issues change policy scope or only repo-local design.  Review whether large issue/evidence volume requires a different issue-ledger architecture.  Review whether compression/archive belongs in policy, runtime, or repo-local tooling.  Challenge A-style assumptions: single-reader process flow, single-writer assumptions, exception-only human review, central-log sufficiency, and “discussion equals approval” drift.  Propose a migration path from prose/evidence files toward a replayable issue ledger.  Record risks and open questions that block treating proposalRevision v1 as implementation-ready.  POSITION  REVISION_REQUIRED.  The main change I would require is: policy should define invariants, not implementation HOWTOs; repo-local issue design must absorb the storage, concurrency, replay, snapshot, archive, and backend-specific mechanics.  Git-managed issues are acceptable, but only if the design explicitly chooses between single-active-writer issue files and multi-writer issue event streams. The retrieved ticket-vs-Beads evidence shows that ticket-like repo-local files are simpler when there is one active writer per ticket, but they silently lose structured dependency updates under concurrent same-item mutation; Beads/Dolt-style substrates are stronger for relation/independent-field concurrency but still do not provide universal conflict-free behavior.   ticket-vs-beads-aligned-matrix  Large issue/evidence volume does change the repo-local design and should modestly change policy. The policy should require an append-only evidence/issue log, replayability, latest-state materialization, and cold archive integrity. It should not mandate a particular storage engine. The JSONL + SQLite PoC is the clearest supporting pattern: JSONL remains the audit log, SQLite is the fast latest-state view, duplicate event replay is ignored, and API reads must not scan JSONL every time.   SPEC  Compression/archive should not change the meaning of issue state. The snapshot lifecycle documents the right split: current state can be served from memory or latest-state indexes, facts remain in JSONL, snapshots make boot fast, and closed segments before the snapshot boundary can become cold while remaining available for audit/full replay. The runtime-boundary rule is also important: core decides event/reducer/snapshot/segment/cold semantics; runtime adapters decide storage, hashes, compression, and file access.  POLICY_GAPS  No explicit evidence-state taxonomy. Policy should distinguish raw_evidence, candidate_summary, adopted_policy, rejected, deprecated, hold, and out_of_scope. Without that, discussion artifacts and derived summaries can accidentally become normative.  No clear approval boundary. The policy must state that file upload, readback, thread reply, generated report, branch inventory, or issue-ledger record does not authorize merge, push, cleanup, branch deletion, issue closure, or implementation acceptance.  Git-managed issue backend is under-specified. Policy should require each repo to declare its issue-backend mode:  single-writer: one active claim/lease per issue, strict CAS/update check, no same-issue multi-agent writes.  multi-writer: field/relation-level conflict surfacing, replay tests, and explicit merge semantics.  hybrid: append-only comments/evidence are multi-writer; issue status/ownership/deps are guarded by claim/CAS.  Large-volume behavior is not policy-visible enough. Policy should define invariant-level requirements: append-only source of truth, materialized latest view, replay, duplicate idempotence, segmenting, snapshot manifest, hash verification, and full replay audit. It should not say “use SQLite” globally, but it should permit or require a latest-state view once raw-log reads become operationally unsafe.  Archive/compression semantics need a boundary. Policy should say compression is allowed only for closed/cold segments after snapshot boundary and only if hash/manifest/full-replay restore remain valid. It should not let compression become deletion, nor let runtime compression details leak into policy semantics.  Worst-case Git publish failures are not elevated enough. The repo design needs policy-visible invariants for partial issue/code publish divergence, closed-issue resurrection, origin ref deletion/rename, and toolchain drift. The worst-case simulations already call out these exact failure modes for refs/issues/*, stale closed issues, ref deletion/rename, and git-native-issue/awk drift.   urn__spec__worst_case_simulatio…  Policy appears vulnerable to package-detail capture. If v1 embeds package HOWTOs, WebMCP details, ops-cdp-core operational steps, or forge-specific commands as policy, it will overfit. Those belong in package contracts or repo-local runbooks. Policy should retain only authority, provenance, replay, approval, and migration invariants.  REPO_DESIGN_GAPS  Canonical issue state needs an event layer. A repo-local issue design should not rely only on mutable Markdown issue files. Use an append-only event stream as source of truth, then generate Markdown, dashboards, SQLite/latest views, and summaries.  Suggested repo shape:  issues/events/*.jsonl — canonical issue/evidence events.  issues/views/latest.sqlite or generated issues/views/latest/*.json — derived latest-state view, never canonical.  issues/snapshots/manifest.json — snapshot pointer, hash, applied sequence, cold boundary.  issues/snapshots/*.json or compressed runtime output — canonical snapshot payload.  issues/archive/cold/* — compressed closed segments, hash-addressed.  issues/evidence-ledger.jsonl — artifact path/hash/type/readability/caveat/source classification.  issues/generated/*.md — readable reports, indexes, issue pages; generated only.  tools/issue-ledger — append, replay, fsck, snapshot, verify-archive, materialize.  Latest-state reads must not scan all evidence. The JSONL + SQLite PoC already demonstrates tail ingest, duplicate protection, package latest-state tables, and replay into a fresh DB. That pattern should be ported to issue state if evidence volume is expected to grow.   SPEC  Snapshot and cold archive must be first-class. The current design should adopt the snapshot lifecycle boundary: snapshot stores canonical state plus applied sequence, derived indexes are rebuilt, and old logs can be cold only after snapshot boundary.   SNAPSHOT_LIFECYCLE  Compression must live below semantic core. Runtime can decide gzip/zstd/file storage, but repo policy/core must decide what is eligible for cold compaction. This prevents “we compressed it” from becoming “we changed or deleted evidence.”   RUNTIME_BOUNDARY  Concurrency model must be explicit before multi-agent use. If the repo uses ticket-like Markdown/YAML issue files, then same-issue multi-agent writes should be disallowed by policy and tooling. If same-issue parallelism is required, use an event or database-backed substrate with explicit contention behavior.   ticket-vs-beads-aligned-matrix  Git publication needs post-push verification. One push containing code and issue refs is not enough unless the remote is compared after publication. The partial-publish simulation shows the failure: code branch push can succeed while refs/issues/* push fails, leaving fixed code and open issue state diverged.   urn__spec__worst_case_simulatio…  Generated views must be treated as disposable. Markdown issue pages, dashboards, summaries, and review packets are views. They should be rebuildable from events + snapshots + evidence ledger.  MIGRATION_PLAN  Freeze v1 as discussion evidence, not policy adoption. Record proposalRevision v1, actor issue-policy-review-B, discussion id, timestamp, source hash if available, and retrieval caveat. Do not mark implementation accepted.  Create a source-artifact ledger. For each Project Source artifact, record: path/name, hash, type, source status, readable/unreadable flag, extracted summary, caveats, and whether it is raw_evidence, candidate_summary, adopted, rejected, deprecated, hold, or out_of_scope.  Define issue event schema. Minimum fields: schema_version, event_id, stream_seq, issue_id, event_type, actor_id, occurred_at, repo, proposal_revision, parent_event_ids, payload, source_refs, idempotency_key, and cas_base for guarded mutations.  Implement replay and fsck before migration. The first implementation target should be deterministic replay into a latest-state view, duplicate-event ignore, missing-parent detection, hash verification, and generated Markdown report output.  Add latest-state materialization. Start with in-memory or JSON view for small repos. Move to SQLite once issue count, evidence count, or query needs justify it. The JSONL + SQLite evidence supports this as the scalable shape, but SQLite should be treated as derived state.   SPEC  Add snapshot lifecycle. Segment logs, snapshot canonical state, update manifest last, and prove boot from snapshot + tail replay. Cold archive only after replay verification.  Choose issue backend mode. For A-style process, I would default to single-writer-per-issue + append-only evidence comments unless the team explicitly needs same-issue multi-agent mutation. If same-issue mutation is required, ticket-like files are the wrong default.  Migrate old issue/evidence material. Convert existing Markdown issues, discussion comments, branch inventories, logs, and review packets into event records. Preserve original raw artifacts externally or in cold storage by hash; do not copy full raw logs into policy files.  Rewrite policy after schema exists. Keep policy small: authority, provenance, approval boundary, event source-of-truth, latest-view derivation, replay/audit, archive/cold semantics, and backend-declared concurrency mode.  Run migration acceptance tests. Required tests: full replay, duplicate replay, snapshot boot + tail, cold archive restore, partial publish detection, stale closed issue reopen guard, ref deletion denial, toolchain version check, and generated report regeneration.  RISKS  Silent lost update risk. Ticket-like Git files can look safe under one-writer workflows but lose structured updates under concurrent same-item writes.   ticket-vs-beads-aligned-matrix  Issue/code divergence risk. If code refs and issue refs publish separately, a “fixed” code state can coexist with a remote-open issue state.   urn__spec__worst_case_simulatio…  Archive-as-deletion risk. Compression without manifest/hash/replay discipline can become silent evidence loss.  SQLite shadow-truth risk. If any tool mutates SQLite/latest views directly, the append-only event log stops being the source of truth.  A-style overconfidence risk. A-style flows tend to assume the process can classify, route, verify, and archive in one clean path. The blind spot is that misclassification often appears only after contradictory evidence or user challenge. Policy needs explicit self-correction and contradiction capture, not just “review on exception.”  Central-log insufficiency risk. A central log or generated review packet is not enough for large evidence volume. It must be an index into replayable facts, not the fact store.  Same-issue parallelism risk. If multiple agents update one issue, “append comments are safe” does not imply status/deps/claims/closure are safe.  Toolchain drift risk. Git-native issue tooling, shell tools, parsers, hooks, and awk/Git versions can produce local success and CI/restore failure unless pinned and fscked.   urn__spec__worst_case_simulatio…  Policy bloat risk. Putting package-specific runbooks into global policy will make the policy hard to evolve and unsafe to reuse.  Approval laundering risk. Discussion records, project-source readback, generated artifacts, or “review packet created” can be mistaken for approval unless policy forbids that explicitly.  OPEN_QUESTIONS  Is the intended issue backend single active writer per issue, or does v1 require same-issue multi-agent mutation?  Are Git-managed issues stored as tree files, Git refs, JSONL files, Beads/Dolt state, or a hybrid?  Does the project require atomic publication of code state and issue state, or is post-push compare plus repair acceptable?  What is the exact event schema for issue status, evidence attachment, claim, handoff, close, reopen, and archive?  What is the snapshot threshold: event count, byte size, time, issue count, or manual checkpoint?  What is the cold archive restore SLA: immediate local restore, full audit replay, or only forensic recovery?  Are compressed cold segments allowed to leave the main repo, or must every repo clone retain full audit material?  Which policy items are global invariants, and which belong in repo-local package contracts?  What are the minimum fsck checks before any issue closure or branch cleanup?  How should stale patches against closed issues be handled: reject, reopen-required, or create follow-up issue?  Who is allowed to migrate evidence state from candidate_summary to adopted_policy?  What explicit signal upgrades proposalRevision v1 into a later revision ready for implementation review?  How does A-style process detect its own wrong assumptions without waiting for user correction or another session to contradict it?

PEER_REVIEW  Source caveat: I could read THREAD_A_REPLY_V1.md and the uploaded/local THREAD_B_REPLY_V1.md. The exact ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_V1.md file was not directly present in the current upload set, so direct claims about it are based on A’s and B’s quoted references to it rather than an independently opened copy.  1. strongest points from A  A’s strongest point is the control-plane / data-plane split: keep a small Git-managed issue interface for coordination, but do not turn Git into the universal evidence database. A states this directly: Git should hold a durable machine-readable ledger sufficient for worker startup, review, merge, and recovery, but not all historical issues, evidence, and local issue detail under one active issues/*.jsonl gate.   THREAD_A_REPLY_V1  A improves on B by making the issues/*.jsonl glob problem concrete. It identifies that issues/*.jsonl is overloaded as “all issue ledger files,” “current v1 records,” and “complete validation universe,” and says legacy 260519.jsonl causes a full-gate failure while scoped current-v1 validation passes.   THREAD_A_REPLY_V1  A’s proposed active / archive / legacy validation classes are strong. B argued for replay, fsck, snapshots, and archive integrity, but A adds a necessary operational distinction: normal worker startup should not require full-history validation, while release or migration jobs can.   THREAD_A_REPLY_V1  A’s structured evidenceRefs[] proposal is probably the cleanest policy-patch seed in the whole exchange: ref, kind, sha256, sizeBytes, storageTier, retentionClass, sensitivity, and requiredForClose. This directly addresses large evidence, privacy, artifact reachability, and review burden without requiring bulky evidence to live in Git.   THREAD_A_REPLY_V1  A also catches two important workflow semantics that B underweighted: narrowing after partial resolution and split-vs-supersede rules. A says a partially resolved issue can remain open/ready after narrowing, and that same-issue supersession should be used only when worker-facing problem and close criteria remain continuous.   THREAD_A_REPLY_V1  A’s warning that archive technologies can hide evidence is right: LFS, git-annex, artifact stores, and archive branches may preserve blobs while making them unavailable to a worker unless stable refs, hashes, and retrieval expectations are policy-defined.   THREAD_A_REPLY_V1  2. objections to A  A is correct that Git should not be the evidence data plane, but it risks under-specifying the canonical event/replay layer. B’s position was that repo-local issue design should not rely only on mutable issue files; it needs an append-only event stream, generated views, latest-state materialization, snapshots, archive verification, and fsck/replay acceptance tests.   THREAD_B_REPLY_V1  A’s “latest active issue record plus repo policy” invariant is useful but insufficient by itself. A must still say what proves that the latest record was derived correctly: event ordering, duplicate-event idempotence, supersedes resolution, missing-parent detection, hash verification, and replay determinism. The adjacent JSONL + SQLite design supports this shape: JSONL is the append-only audit log, SQLite is only the fast latest-state view, duplicates are ignored, and API reads should not scan JSONL every time.   SPEC  A discusses merge conflicts but does not fully answer B’s concurrency-model objection. Before multi-agent issue mutation is allowed, policy or repo-local design must declare whether issue state is single-writer, multi-writer event stream, or hybrid. Without that, A’s sharding/manifest advice may reduce line conflicts while still permitting semantic lost updates.  A also underweights issue/code publication divergence. B called out that code can publish while issue refs fail, leaving “fixed code / open issue” remote divergence. A’s validation-mode proposal should add a post-push compare or atomic-publication requirement before closure.  A is weaker on approval laundering. A mentions same-revision no-objections and facilitator summary not being a verdict in open questions, but that belongs in the policy patch candidate, not just an unresolved question. B’s objection remains: upload, readback, generated report, discussion reply, or issue-ledger record must not imply approval, merge permission, cleanup permission, or implementation acceptance.   THREAD_B_REPLY_V1  A labels many items as “policy-rule-change candidate.” That is useful for agenda enumeration, but the policy patch should not absorb repo-local HOWTO. B’s boundary should stand: global policy defines invariants; repo-local design chooses paths, storage, tools, manifests, validation commands, and migration mechanics.   THREAD_B_REPLY_V1  3. agenda items to add/remove/rename  Add: “Issue backend and concurrency mode.” This should force a repo to declare single-writer, multi-writer, or hybrid issue mutation semantics before same-issue multi-agent work.  Add: “Evidence state taxonomy and approval boundary.” A has evidence storage; B has evidence-state and approval-laundering concerns. Combine them: raw evidence, candidate summary, adopted policy, rejected, deprecated, hold, and out-of-scope must not be confused with approval.  Add: “Replay, snapshot, fsck, and latest-state proof.” A’s active/latest worker invariant needs a proof path. Latest records should be reproducible from canonical events or clearly marked as authoritative superseding records.  Add: “Publication divergence and post-push verification.” Issue state and code state can diverge when Git publication partially succeeds. This is separate from validation and must be tested.  Rename: “Should issues live inside Git-managed repo paths at all?” → “What issue control plane belongs in Git?” A’s own answer is not “no Git issues”; it is “small control plane in Git, bulky evidence outside Git.” The renamed agenda better matches the conclusion.  Rename: “Does append-only JSONL make repo volume grow too much?” → “What lifecycle bounds append-only ledgers?” The issue is not append-only itself; it is segmentation, snapshotting, compaction, archive restore, and validation class.  Rename: “Should validation always cover all issues/*.jsonl?” → “Which validation mode applies at worker startup, release, migration, and audit?” A’s strongest contribution is multiple gate meanings. The agenda should encode those modes explicitly.  Remove or demote: “Should compression remove the concern?” Compression is a mechanism, not the real question. The real agenda item is archive integrity, restore SLA, worker availability, and whether compression changes semantics. A’s own risk section says compression reduces size but not governance burden.   THREAD_A_REPLY_V1  4. whether v1 should become a policy patch, repo-local design task, migration task, or remain discussion-only  v1-peer should not become one monolithic policy patch.  It should be split as follows:  Policy patch candidate:  Minimal cross-repo issue interface.  Structured evidenceRefs[].  Active/archive/legacy validation classes.  Evidence retention and sensitivity classes.  Approval boundary: discussion/readback/generated artifacts do not approve implementation or merge.  Blocked-scope semantics.  Split-vs-supersede and narrowing semantics at invariant level.  Requirement that each repo declares an issue backend/concurrency mode.  Repo-local design task:  Choose manifest vs path layout: issues/active, issues/archive, issues/legacy, issues/evidence, or equivalent.  Define local issue schema projection to the minimal interface.  Define event stream, generated views, latest-state materialization, fsck, replay, snapshot, archive, and restore commands.  Define post-push verification for issue/code state.  Migration task:  Quarantine or manifest-exclude 260519.jsonl as legacy evidence.  Preserve the scoped passing 260524.jsonl + 260525.jsonl + 260526.jsonl active chain.  Add a v1 legacy-index/migration-note record.  Backfill indexes, not rewritten history.  Add validation modes before broad migration. A’s migration plan already sketches this.   THREAD_A_REPLY_V1  Discussion-only until split: The current v1 should remain discussion-only as a bundle. It becomes actionable only after the policy patch, repo-local design task, and migration task are separated and each has acceptance criteria.  5. unresolved objections  The exact ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_V1.md file still needs a direct reread before any patch is accepted; A and B both quote it, but this peer review should not treat quoted references as a substitute for the source file.  The project has not chosen the issue backend mode: single-writer issue files, multi-writer event streams, or hybrid guarded fields plus append-only evidence/comments.  The canonical source of truth is still ambiguous: latest active issue record, append-only event log, superseding authoritative record, or generated/materialized view.  Active-only validation is necessary for worker usability, but not sufficient for safety. Release, migration, and audit gates must detect broken archives, missing evidence refs, stale supersedes, and hidden obligations.  Structured evidence refs solve naming and metadata, but not restore authority. The project still needs artifact-store credentials policy, cold archive restore SLA, required-vs-optional evidence behavior, and secret/sensitivity handling.  A’s agenda does not fully handle issue/code publish divergence. Closure should require either atomic publication or post-push comparison proving issue state and code state are synchronized.  Approval laundering remains open. Same-revision no-objections, facilitator summaries, generated reports, file uploads, and readbacks must be evidence, not verdicts.  Split-vs-supersede needs test cases. The NO_UNRESOLVED_OBJECTIONS marker bug and the narrowed Project Source issue are good candidates, but policy should specify expected behavior before migration.  Compression and archive remain semantic traps. Compaction must be derived unless explicitly reviewed as an authoritative superseding record; otherwise archive tooling can silently rewrite audit history.  The A-style blind spot remains: “full validation over every historical file” is not safety, but “latest active record only” is not safety either. The policy needs layered validation with explicit meanings, not a single ritual gate.
